newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament head wants budget changes.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament head wants budget changes.

text.p: Ukraine's 1997 draft budget must be changed to bring it into line with the new consitution and documents already approved by parliament, the assembly's speaker Olexander Moroz told the chamber on Tuesday.
He gave no indication which changes were required under constitutional law.
But he said the draft turned over to parliament two weeks ago did not provide detailed revenue and expenditure estimates, as demanded by the constitution, and contained about 60 items lacking detail.
He complained the government had given no explanation of how much it hoped to receive in foreign credits in the coming year.
Ukraine's parliament, where Communists and their allies make up the largest bloc, is likely to pass the budget, but ministers could be prompted to make changes.

The draft states that the projected deficit will be covered by 2.09 billion hryvnias in foreign credits and 200 billion credits in internal credits -- printing money or funds raised by the sale of securities. But it gives no further details.

The draft foresees a deficit at 3.8 percent of gross domestic product, or two percent by Western methods of calculation, and an annual inflation rate of 24.9 percent compared to a projected 48 percent in 1996.

Mykola Azarov, head of parliament's budget committee, has said parliament might change some of the indicators detailed in the budget draft. Parliament also asked President Leonid Kuchma to report to deputies on Ukraine's social and economic situation on October 8. But Kuchma is scheduled to visit Spain then. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Bureau, +380 44 229 2264
